pages.text: High above the Platonic Realm's own islands (the Number Line), across a gap of empty air, and far below Curved Space lies the $(thing)Elements$(): islands of $(item)Euclidean Marble$() from Y 320 to 400, laid out as if with compass and straightedge.
In the Realm, sneak and use the $(item)Platonic Compass$() to climb a layer (sneak and look down to go down one). This is the safe layer: none of the Realm's hunters come up here.

$(thing)Compass Towers$() rise fourteen to twenty-five blocks and carry a circle and the hexagon stepped round it with the same opening (Book IV, Proposition 15). $(thing)Geometer's Ruins$() have Euclid's proof of Pythagoras inlaid in the floor: squares of 144 and 256 on the legs of a right triangle (12 and 16 long), and one of 400 on its long side (20). A cache waits at the right angle. The Platonic solids float here too, in marble.

$(item)Euclid's Automaton$() walks only in straight lines and turns on the spot through angles it can construct. Now and then it makes a construction the way surveyors always have: it drives a pin into the ground, walks once round it with the cord taut (a circle), then walks the six sides of the hexagon inside it, each as long as the cord, its straightedge on the ground. The lines glow for half a minute. Leave it to its work: it fights only whoever hurts it. Struck, it rouses: its eyes burn red and follow you, and steam pours from its shoulders.

$(item)Euclidean Ore$() gives $(item)Euclidean Shards$() (the Automaton drops them too). The Geometer's Table draws a stack of Golden Ratio Glass from plain glass and a single shard (or a bigger stack from eight glass and eight Euclidean Marble), and lays out eight marble from eight cobblestone and a shard; a shard mends a Platonic Compass at an anvil; and the later machines of Mathematics are built with them.
